title: Transport of module objects and projection formulas
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$ be monoidal categories. Monoid objects and module objects
are as in [sk-def-sfb-ring-object] and [sk-def-sfb-module-objects].

1. **Transport along a lax monoidal functor.** Let $F\colon\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be lax
   monoidal, with structure maps $\mu^F_{X,Y}\colon FX\otimes FY\to F(X\otimes Y)$. For a
   monoid object $\mathcal R$ of $\mathcal C$, $F\mathcal R$ is a monoid object of
   $\mathcal D$. An $\mathcal R$-module object $M$ gives the $F\mathcal R$-module object
   $FM$, with action
   $F\mathcal R\otimes FM\xrightarrow{\mu^F}F(\mathcal R\otimes M)\xrightarrow{F\gamma_M}FM$.
   This defines a functor
   $$
   \operatorname{mapMod}(F)\colon\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)\to\Mod_{F\mathcal R}(\mathcal D)
   $$
   that commutes with the forgetful functors.
2. **Monoidal adjunctions.** Let $F\dashv G$ be a monoidal adjunction, with $F$ strong
   monoidal and $G$ lax monoidal, the structures being mates. Then the unit
   $u_{\mathcal R}\colon\mathcal R\to GF\mathcal R$ is a morphism of monoid objects, and,
   with the restriction of scalars of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars],
   $$
   \operatorname{mapMod}(F)\dashv\operatorname{Res}_{u_{\mathcal R}}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(G).
   $$
3. **Projection formulas.** Let $S\colon\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ be strong monoidal and
   $P\colon\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ a functor. A *projection formula* for $P$ relative to
   $S$ is a family of isomorphisms $P(SL\otimes M)\cong L\otimes PM$, natural in $L$ and
   $M$ and compatible with the unit and the associativity constraints. It *linearizes*
   $P$: for every monoid object $\mathcal B$ of $\mathcal D$, it gives a functor
   $$
   P_{\mathcal B}\colon\Mod_{S\mathcal B}(\mathcal C)\to\Mod_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal D),
   \qquad M\mapsto PM,
   $$
   where $\mathcal B$ acts by
   $\mathcal B\otimes PM\cong P(S\mathcal B\otimes M)\xrightarrow{P\gamma_M}PM$. Every
   right adjoint $G$ of $P$ linearizes to a functor
   $G_{\mathcal B}\colon\Mod_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal D)\to\Mod_{S\mathcal B}(\mathcal C)$,
   $N\mapsto GN$, and $P_{\mathcal B}\dashv G_{\mathcal B}$.
4. **Adjunctions $P\dashv S$.** For an adjunction $P\dashv S$ with $S$ strong monoidal, the
   *projection formula map* $P(SL\otimes M)\to L\otimes PM$ is the adjoint of
   $SL\otimes M\to SL\otimes SPM\to S(L\otimes PM)$. If these maps are isomorphisms, they
   form a projection formula. Then $G_{\mathcal B}=\operatorname{mapMod}(S)$, so
   $P_{\mathcal B}\dashv\operatorname{mapMod}(S)$.

proof.text: For part 1 use [def-sfb-modobj-transport] with the given lax monoidal functor $F$ and monoid $\mathcal R$. Its multiplication and unit on $F\mathcal R$ are $F(\mu)\circ\mu^F_{\mathcal R,\mathcal R}$ and $F(\eta)\circ\varepsilon^F$. Its module action is exactly the displayed composite in part 1; its morphism assignment is $f\mapsto Ff$. The cited construction gives both module axioms, linearity of this assignment and the equality of the underlying functors, hence the stated functor commuting with forgetful functors.

For part 2 the hypotheses are precisely those of [def-sfb-modobj-transport-adjunction]: $F$ is strong monoidal and the lax structure on $G$ is its adjoint mate. That statement makes $u_{\mathcal R}$ a monoid morphism and restricts the original adjunction bijection to $F\mathcal R$-linear maps $FM\to N$ and $\mathcal R$-linear maps $M\to GN$, with the latter action restricted through $u_{\mathcal R}$. These natural bijections give exactly the adjunction of part 2.

For part 3 the coherent natural isomorphisms are the data of [def-sfb-projection-formula]. Apply [def-sfb-modobj-linearization] to these data and the given monoid $\mathcal B$: its action is $P(\gamma_M)\circ\pi^{-1}_{\mathcal B,M}$, its maps are $Pf$, and its source is modules over the transported monoid $S\mathcal B$. Thus it supplies precisely $P_{\mathcal B}$ and the displayed action; no commutativity of $\mathcal B$ is required.

source.place: paragraph 2, projection formula and left linearization

proof.text: Given any specified adjunction $P\dashv G$ with counit $c$, [def-sfb-modobj-linearization-right-adjoint] defines $\theta_{L,N}:SL\otimes GN\to G(L\otimes N)$ as the mate of $(L\otimes c_N)\circ\pi_{L,GN}$ and gives the action $G(\gamma_N)\circ\theta_{\mathcal B,N}$ on $GN$. This gives $G_{\mathcal B}$ on objects and on morphisms. The statement [def-sfb-modobj-linearized-adjunction] restricts the same adjunction bijection to the two kinds of linear maps and gives $P_{\mathcal B}\dashv G_{\mathcal B}$. This proves the remaining assertions of part 3.

For part 4 apply [def-sfb-adjunction-has-projection-formula] to the specified adjunction $P\dashv S$: the mate defining its projection formula map is exactly $\mu^S_{L,PM}\circ(SL\otimes u_M)$. When those maps are isomorphisms, [def-sfb-adjunction-projection-formula] asserts their naturality and their unit and associativity compatibilities, so they supply the projection formula required in part 3.

source.place: paragraph 3, canonical map and coherent projection formula

proof.text: Identify the right linearization in part 4 explicitly. Put $G=S$ in [def-sfb-modobj-linearization-right-adjoint] and write $c$ for the counit of $P\dashv S$. By the mate formula in [def-sfb-adjunction-has-projection-formula], naturality of the adjunction bijection in its target gives $\theta_{L,N}=S(L\otimes c_N)\circ\mu^S_{L,PSN}\circ(SL\otimes u_{SN})$. Naturality of $\mu^S$ rewrites this as $\mu^S_{L,N}\circ(SL\otimes(S(c_N)\circ u_{SN}))=\mu^S_{L,N}$ by the triangle identity. Hence the action on $SN$ is $S(\gamma_N)\circ\mu^S_{\mathcal B,N}$, exactly the action of [def-sfb-modobj-transport]; both functors send a morphism $f$ to $Sf$. Thus $G_{\mathcal B}=\operatorname{mapMod}(S)$ as claimed.

source.place: paragraph 3, identification of the right linearization; expanded mate computation

proof.text: With this identification, the adjunction $P_{\mathcal B}\dashv G_{\mathcal B}$ of [def-sfb-modobj-linearized-adjunction] is $P_{\mathcal B}\dashv\operatorname{mapMod}(S)$. Its hom bijection takes a $\mathcal B$-linear map $PM\to N$ to its original adjoint $M\to SN$, which is the construction specified by [def-sfb-modobj-linearization-transport-adjunction]. This proves the last assertion of part 4.
